;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2020 Iranian attack on U.S. forces in Iraq]]
**[[Iran]] begins [[Operation Martyr Soleimani]], launching [[ballistic missile]]s at several [[United States Armed Forces]] facilities in [[Iraq]], including [[Al Asad Airbase]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/iran-launches-missiles-us-air-bases-iraq-us/story?id=68130625 (ABC News)]
**Iran's [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] issues a statement warning regional countries not to allow the [[United States]] military to launch attacks on Iran from their territory or they "will be targeted". [https://apnews.com/add7a702258b4419d796aa5f48e577fc (Associated Press)]
**In response to Iranian missile attacks on U.S. forces, the U.S. [[Federal Aviation Administration]] (FAA) bans all U.S. commercial flights from operating in airspace over Iraq, Iran, the [[Persian Gulf]] and the [[Gulf of Oman]]. [https://www.jpost.com/Middle-East/FAA-bans-flights-over-Iraq-Iran-Gulf-of-Oman-after-Iranian-attack-613484 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**Due to heightened tensions, [[Japanese Prime Minister]] [[Shinzō Abe]] cancels his scheduled trips to [[Saudi Arabia]], the [[United Arab Emirates]] and [[Oman]], and convenes a National Security Council meeting, likely to discuss Iran's attack on U.S. forces based in Iraq. [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/01/08/world/middleeast/07reuters-iraq-security-japan-abe.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces new sanctions against Iran in response to the attack. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2020/01/08/us-officials-warned-missile-launch-iraq-bases-troops/2842200001/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**An [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] [[car bomb|car bombing]] kills six people and injures 12 others at an [[Somali Armed Forces|army]] [[security checkpoint|checkpoint]] near [[Somalia]]'s [[Parliament of Somalia|parliament]] in [[Mogadishu]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-01-08/six-killed-in-car-bomb-attack-in-somalia-s-capital-police-say (Bloomberg News)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**A car bomb kills four [[Turkey Armed Forces|Turkish soldiers]] when a vehicle explodes at a checkpoint during a road check in northeastern Syria. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1610276/middle-east (''Arab News'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex|Prince Harry]] and his wife [[Meghan, Duchess of Sussex|Meghan]] announce their plan to "step back as 'senior' members" of the [[British royal family]]. [[Buckingham Palace]] says discussions on the intended new role are "at an early stage". [https://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/2020/01/08/Prince-Harry-Meghan-Markle-step-back-from-royal-family/7241578509912/ (United Press International)]

;Business and economy
*[[Tesla, Inc.]] reports a stock [[market capitalization]] of [[U.S. dollar|US$]]88 billion in response to strong performances in the third- and fourth-[[Fiscal year|quarter]], surpassing [[General Motors]] and [[Ford Motor Company]] to become the most valuable [[Automotive industry|automobile company]] in [[North America]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-stocks-tesla/teslas-market-value-eclipses-gm-and-ford-combined-idUSKBN1Z72MU (Reuters)] [https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/tesla-stock-price-rally-most-valuable-us-car-maker-history-2020-1-1028804022 (''Business Insider'')]
*The heads of state of [[Turkey]], [[Russia]], [[Serbia]] and [[Bulgaria]] formally inaugurate the [[TurkStream]] gas pipelines. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-russia-pipeline/turkey-russia-launch-turkstream-pipeline-carrying-gas-to-europe-idUSKBN1Z71WP (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752]]
**A [[Boeing 737 Next Generation#737-800|Boeing 737-800]] crashes while taking off from [[Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport]], killing all 176 people on board. The incident, which took place amid the 2019–20 Persian Gulf crisis, is under investigation.  [https://www.npr.org/2020/01/07/794430621/jetliner-reportedly-carrying-180-people-crashes-near-tehran-airport (NPR)]

;International relations
*[[Norway]] agrees to take in 600 refugees from [[Rwanda]] who were previously evacuated from [[Libya|Libyan]] detention camps. Rwanda last September signed an agreement with the [[United Nations]] to take in [[asylum seeker]]s from Libya while their status was being processed, to cut down on [[human trafficking]] in the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-refugees-rwanda-norway/norway-to-take-600-libya-evacuees-from-rwanda-camp-idUSKBN1Z72IJ?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*Aftermath of the [[Sagamihara stabbings]]
**The trial of Satoshi Uematsu, a young Japanese man who admitted to stabbing 19 [[disabled people]] to death at a care center in 2016, begins. The rampage ranks among the country's worst mass killings. His lawyer is expected to enter a plea of not guilty on grounds of diminished capacity. Uematsu will be handed a sentence on March 16 and could receive the [[capital punishment in Japan|death penalty]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/trial-opens-in-japan-for-grisly-murder-of-19-at-disabled-home-12242124 (CNA)]
*One person is shot dead and three seriously wounded in a shooting near [[Parliament Hill]] in [[Ottawa]]. [[Ottawa Police Service|Police]] believe the shooting was targeted. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-canada-shooting/gunfire-near-canadian-parliament-kills-one-wounds-three-idUSKBN1Z722C (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*[[Kuwait|Kuwaitian]] state news agency [[Kuwait News Agency|KUNA]] says its official [[Twitter]] account was hacked after it spread a [[fake news]] report that the [[United States Army]] would withdraw from [[Camp Arifjan]] within three days. [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/hacked-kuwait-govt-says-report-of-u-s-troop-withdrawal-is-incorrect-1.8373707 (''Haaretz'')]
*[[List of fast radio bursts]]
**Scientists announce through the journal [[Nature (journal)|''Nature'']] the discovery of a repeating [[fast radio burst]] known as [[Fast_radio_burst#FRB_180916|FRB 180916]] coming from a nearby [[spiral galaxy]] around 500 million [[light year]]s from [[Earth]]. It is the second repeating FRB to have been localized. [https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/gadgets-and-tech/news/radio-signal-frb-galaxy-space-universe-fast-burst-a9273356.html (''The Independent'')]
